Unlike linear inclusion functions, which only bound the function value based on the first derivative, QTIFs incorporate the second-order Lipschitz constant of the derivative to bound the function value [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that quadratic Taylor inclusion functions are used for functions whose derivative is Lipschitz continuous, and they utilize the second-order Lipschitz constant (denoted as $gamma = Lip(f')$) to bound the function value. The formula provided in the evidence, $[f](t) = f(t_0) + (t - t_0) ( f'(t_0) pm frac{1}{2} gamma(t - t_0) )$, confirms that the bound depends on the first derivative $f'(t_0)$ and the second-order Lipschitz constant $gamma$. In contrast, linear inclusion functions typically rely only on the first derivative (and a first-order Lipschitz constant for the function itself, or just the slope for linear approximation). The claim accurately reflects that QTIFs incorporate the second-order Lipschitz constant of the derivative to bound the function value, distinguishing them from simpler linear bounds.
